sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Collierville?
sections.html:
A Collierville house is taxed by two bodies: the Town of Collierville and Shelby County. The town's tax department answers questions at 901-457-2281 or propertytax@colliervilletn.gov, and residents owe county tax in addition to the town's.

On the county side, the Assessor of Property establishes value, the Board of Commissioners picks the county rate, and the Trustee prints the notices and mails them to whatever address the Assessor holds. If a lender escrows your taxes, the servicer may request the figures and pay the bill, but the Trustee still advises borrowers to keep the original notice.

Because the notice follows the Assessor's mailing address, anyone who has moved should update it well before October.

sections.h2: How a Collierville tax bill is figured
sections.html:
The town rate is $1.62 for each $100 of assessed value. Tennessee assesses homes at 25% of appraisal, so the town bill is a quarter of the appraised value times that rate, divided by 100.

Other classes use different percentages: 40% for commercial and industrial parcels, 55% for public utilities, 25% for farms and 30% for personal property. Add the Shelby County rate on top, which the Trustee or the Assessor can quote for your parcel. With a median owner-occupied value of $485,900, a typical Collierville assessment is large even before the county share is added.

County bills can be paid from the first Monday of October, and no interest builds before the end of February.

Collierville is in the group whose bills turn delinquent March 1. Unpaid base tax then gains 1.5% a month, which the Trustee states as 18% a year. Mail a check with the stub from your notice to the Shelby County Trustee, P.O. Box 2751, Memphis, TN 38101-2751, and make sure the postmark is no later than the last day of February.

Call Trustee customer service at (901) 222-0200 with account questions. Tenn. Code Ann. 67-5-2405 requires the Trustee to sue for delinquent real estate tax. The parcel carries a tax lien until the whole balance is cleared.

sections.h2: How to appeal your Collierville assessment
sections.html:
The usual path begins with an informal review at the Assessor's office. A formal filing with the Board of Equalization comes only if the review leaves you unconvinced. An informal review is not an appeal. It gives you a chance to hand over information so the value tracks the market.

Where a Collierville value dispute goes next
StepTimingWhere
Informal reviewCloses on the last day of MayShelby County Assessor of Property
County board appealTypically closes the last working day of JuneBoard of Equalization, 901-222-7300
State board appealAugust 1, or 45 days following the county notice if that is laterState Board of Equalization, 615-401-7883
CourtFinal stepShelby County Chancery Court

These dates repeat every year, so a dispute filed after they pass waits for the next cycle.

sections.h2: What documents help in a value dispute?
sections.html:
Evidence that points to market value carries the most weight with the Assessor. For a Collierville house, these help:

  • Nearby sale prices of comparable homes from the two years before the tax year at issue.
  • A private appraisal done recently.
  • Interior and exterior photographs showing condition.
  • For income property, three years of income and expense records.

A single median hides a wide spread of values, so lean on sales from your own neighborhood.

The town had about 51,909 residents in mid-2025 and sits in the Memphis metropolitan area, with its own school district, Collierville Schools. The 2020 count was 51,324. Survey results for 2020 to 2024 show 79.9% of homes lived in by owners, $485,900 as the middle owner-occupied value and $1,691 as typical gross rent. Buyers here tend to ask about the roof and storm history, so gather those records before listing.

The title company settles any open balance at closing, so get payoff figures from both the Shelby County Trustee and the town's tax department ahead of time. The Trustee verifies each payoff on the day the money arrives, and the owner is liable for charges through that day.

Read the purchase contract and settlement statement to see who covers the current year's tax.

If you are behind, interest piles up each month from March 1 and a lien stays on the parcel until you clear the balance. Calling the town and the Trustee for a payoff is the right first move.

A cash sale does not change any of this. The title company still needs two payoff letters, and the settlement statement should show the town and county amounts on separate lines. Having them early keeps the closing date from slipping.

sections.h2: A year of Collierville property tax, month by month
sections.html:
Knowing the calendar helps a seller decide when to list and what to expect at closing.

  • Through May: the informal review window is open at the Shelby County Assessor, and it closes on the last day of May.
  • June: the county Board of Equalization appeal usually closes on the last working day of the month.
  • August 1: the general state board deadline, unless 45 days after the county notice is later.
  • First Monday of October: bills open for payment from the town and the county.
  • End of February: last day to pay without interest. A mailed check needs a postmark by then.
  • March 1: unpaid base tax becomes delinquent and starts gaining 1.5% a month.

A house that closes in the middle of this calendar still has a tax bill attached to it, which is why the settlement statement matters so much.

sections.h2: What to have ready for the title company
sections.html:
A little preparation shortens the payoff process. Before you accept an offer, collect the following.

  • The latest town notice and the latest Shelby County notice, with the original stubs if you still have them.
  • Proof of the address the Assessor holds for you, since notices follow it.
  • Your lender's escrow statement, if a servicer pays the taxes from an escrow account.
  • Any paperwork from a value dispute, including the date of an informal review or county board hearing.

The title company will ask the Trustee at (901) 222-0200 and the town at 901-457-2281 for payoff figures. A surprise balance at either office should be settled before the contract date. The lien does not go away until everything owed is paid.

faqs.q: When are Collierville property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first Monday of October opens the payment period. Interest does not start until March 1, so the 2026 bill is on time through the end of February 2027.

faqs.q: What is the Collierville town property tax rate?
faqs.a: The town rate is $1.62 for each $100 of assessed value, applied at the state's 25% residential ratio. Shelby County bills its own rate on top, and the Trustee or the Assessor can tell you what it is for your parcel.

faqs.q: What interest applies if I pay a Collierville tax bill late?
faqs.a: Unpaid base tax accrues 1.5% a month starting March 1, which is 18% a year. The Shelby County Trustee uses the same rate for Collierville, Arlington, Lakeland, Millington, Memphis and the county itself.

faqs.q: Is the informal review the same as an appeal?
faqs.a: No. A review is a chance to pass along information so values match the market, and many disputes end there. An actual appeal is filed with the Shelby County Board of Equalization, typically by the last working day of June.

faqs.q: Whom should I call with a Collierville tax question?
faqs.a: Call the town's tax department at 901-457-2281 for town billing, and Shelby County Trustee customer service at (901) 222-0200 for county balances. For value questions, contact the Shelby County Assessor, or the Board of Equalization at 901-222-7300 once you are ready to file a formal appeal.
